## Overview
This PR establishes the foundational architecture for the token-sync system, implementing a comprehensive framework for synchronizing tokenized assets across the Stacks blockchain. The system provides secure token tracking, prevents double-spending, and enables standardized cross-contract token interactions through five core smart contracts.

## Changes
Added new core contracts:

- **token-registry**: Central source of truth for token relationships and mappings across the ecosystem
- **token-synchronizer**: Manages synchronization operations between token representations while maintaining consistency
- **auth-manager**: Handles authentication and permission management for system security
- **event-tracker**: Records system events for transparency and auditability
- **token-adapter**: Provides standardized interface for different token implementations

Key features implemented:
- Secure token registration and relationship tracking
- Controlled synchronization operations with double-spend prevention
- Comprehensive permission and authentication system
- Event logging for all operations
- Flexible token standard support

## Documentation
Added extensive documentation in README.md including:
- Detailed architecture overview
- Contract descriptions and sample function signatures
- Security measures and considerations
- Usage instructions and deployment order
- Integration guidelines for different token standards

The documentation provides clear guidance for developers looking to integrate with or build upon the token-sync framework.

As discussed in issue #2332 this pull request enables the possibility to login via a jwt token that can be verified by an oidc identity provider.  Hawkbit would act as an oidc resourceserver in this case.

* Added new configuration file [OidcProperties.java](https://github.com/blue-zone-at/hawkbit/blob/ad1d62a58df5e95d30ebbe672aadc31c944f1bae/hawkbit-mgmt/hawkbit-mgmt-starter/src/main/java/org/eclipse/hawkbit/oidc/OidcProperties.java), if there is a better location for this please tell me - i've not found specific configuration properties for the mgmt part.
  * "hawkbit.server.security.oauth2.resourceserver.default-enabled" which defaults to false. If this is false the current behaviour of integrating the hawkbitOAuth2ResourceServerCustomizer works as it does now. If this is true a new default oauth2 resource server configuration is loaded.
  * "hawkbit.server.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.claim.roles" which defaults to "roles". This defines the claim within the jwt token that supplies the hawkbit permissions. For example when using keycloak this can be "resource_access.client-id.roles".
  * "hawkbit.server.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.claim.username" which defaults to "preferred_username". This defines the claim within the jwt token that supplies the hawkbit username.
  * "hawkbit.server.security.oauth2.resourceserver.jwt.claim.tenant" which defaults to null. This defines the claim within the jwt token that supplies the hawkbit tenant. If it is default null the DEFAULT tenant is used for every user.
* Use the existing spring configuration for the resource server as described here: [Spring Documentation](https://docs.spring.io/spring-security/reference/servlet/oauth2/resource-server/jwt.html#oauth2resourceserver-jwt-authorization)
* Add a new Customizer class inside MgmtSecurityConfiguration.java which implements this default OAuth2ResourceServerCustomizer.

body:
### New Features and Improvements

- **`calcFloorspacePast`** and **`calcDensity`**  
  Introduce `endOfHistory` parameter.

- **Remove old U-value read and calc functions**  
  Old and out-phased source read functions `readETSAP` and `readEUBuildingsObservatory` as well as `calcUvalueSource` were removed. 

- **Read and convert MESSAGEix-Buildings data**  
  The function `readMessageIXBuildings` reads regional U-value estimates or cohort-specific floor space estimates from the MESSAGEix-Buildings model, and `convertMessageIXBuildings` converts them into ISO countries. This data gives us U-value estimates for regions outside the EU.

- **`calcUvalueParameters`**  
  Adds a new function to estimate regional fit parameters for projecting building envelope U-values. It uses mixed-effects regression combining historical data from Hotmaps, MESSAGEix-Buildings, and the EU Buildings Observatory, incorporating climate (HDD, CDD) and economic (GDP per capita) indicators. Average U-values are calculated from multiple sources and aggregated using component areas (walls, roofs, windows, floor) as well as vintage- and building-type-specific floor space as weights.

  The regression model is of the form:
$$\log(U - U_\text{min}) = \beta_0 + \beta_1 \cdot HDD + \beta_2 \cdot CDD + \beta_3 \cdot \log(\text{GDPpc} + 1) + \beta_4 \cdot \text{HDD} \cdot \log(\text{GDPpc} + 1) + \beta_5 \cdot \text{CDD} \cdot \log(\text{GDPpc} + 1) + b_r$$
  where $b_r \sim \mathcal{N}(0, \sigma^2_r)$ captures region-specific random effects.

  The function handles regional parameter estimation in two ways:  
  1. For regions with sufficient historical data points, parameters are directly estimated via mixed-effects regression (`lmer`).  
  2. For regions with insufficient data, the function:  
     - Uses global fixed effects as a baseline  
     - Calculates the difference between aggregated regional projections and their reference values  
     - Applies empirical Bayes shrinkage to balance between global pattern and regional differences  
     - Adjusts intercepts using these shrunken offsets to create region-specific parameters  
    
  This will make an adjustment of the projections (lambda) in EDGE-B obsolete, since the trajectories are already shifted correctly by the respective data variance. EDGE-B will now only need to deal with a smoothing of the (historical) data and ensure that U-values are not increasing over time.

## Overview
This PR establishes the foundational smart contract architecture for Pulse DAO, creating a comprehensive governance system specifically designed for healthcare cooperatives. The implementation enables secure member management, healthcare-specific proposal creation, democratic voting mechanisms, and transparent treasury management while maintaining necessary privacy controls for sensitive health information.

## Changes
Added four new core smart contracts that form the governance framework:

### membership-registry
- Implements member verification and role management (Patient, Provider, Admin)
- Handles membership lifecycle including applications, renewals, and terminations
- Establishes role-based permissions and voting power calculation

### proposal-manager
- Enables creation of healthcare-specific governance proposals 
- Implements proposal categories (Facility Improvement, Care Protocol, etc)
- Manages proposal lifecycle with sponsorship system
- Includes privacy controls for sensitive health information

### voting-engine
- Provides multiple voting mechanisms (simple majority, quadratic, role-weighted)
- Implements vote delegation and quorum requirements
- Ensures vote privacy for sensitive decisions
- Maintains auditable voting records

### treasury-controller
- Manages cooperative financial resources and distributions
- Implements emergency fund provisions for urgent healthcare needs
- Handles recurring expenses and maintains audit trail
- Provides transparent fund allocation reporting

## Documentation
Added comprehensive README documentation covering:
- Detailed overview of the DAO architecture
- Description of all core components and their interactions
- Contract-specific features and capabilities
- Setup and deployment instructions
- Key security considerations and privacy controls

body:
Resolves #142. See also the discussion at https://github.com/linebender/vello/pull/830#discussion_r1982017666.

On x86, `f32::round` is slow as it calls out to the IEEE754-adhering libc function `roundf`. See, e.g., the branchy [glibc `roundf`](https://sourceware.org/git/?p=glibc.git;a=blob;f=sysdeps/ieee754/flt-32/s_roundf.c;h=eb714e975e48f737c140a1dd666135759ac0ffe3;hb=HEAD) and [musl `roundf`](https://git.etalabs.net/cgit/musl/tree/src/math/roundf.c?h=c47ad25ea3b484e10326f933e927c0bc8cded3da) implementations. On AArch64, the compiler can make use of hardware instructions instead.

The knowledge that the output range is `0-255`, allows writing an almost-correct rounding implementation that doesn't require calling out to libc or branching. This is fast on both x86 and AArch64.

Codegen:
x86: https://godbolt.org/z/PaEP43fGP
AArch64: https://godbolt.org/z/vd9Wcjz6q

`$this->getSpecialPrice()` and `$this->getTierPrice()` Return a converted price when using multiple currencies, however these prices there converted again a little bit further down the function

prices are only converted when necessary so they are only converted once.
